solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Artist whose career is taking off? (13)

annotation.definition: Artist whose career is taking off?

blocks.note: the surface wants a painter; the setter also means a stage performer
the surface reading is a rising career; the setter's reading is 'taking off' as imitating people

annotation.surface: A painter whose career is about to soar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' reads as a career on the rise, but it means mimicking: an impressionist is also an entertainer who imitates famous people, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An impressionist is both a Monet-style painter and a mimic whose whole job is taking people off.

entries.clue: Suggested independent member was being economical with the truth (7)

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for independent
Member of Parliament

blocks.clueFragment: was being economical with the truth
blocks.note: a famous euphemism for lying

annotation.surface: A proposed independent MP turns out to have been lying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being economical with the truth' is a well-known British political euphemism for lying, which suits the MP perfectly.
annotation.definitionFit: Implied means suggested without being stated outright.

entries.clue: Scattered, leaderless, break down (5)

indicators.note: without its leader: the first letter goes

blocks.note: sparse means thinly scattered; drop the S

annotation.surface: A scattered group without a leader falls apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break down' reads as collapse, but it is the grammarian's sense: to parse a sentence is to break it down into its parts.
annotation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to break it down into its grammatical parts.

entries.clue: Collective symbol of masculinity alienating male extremists (8)

indicators.note: pushing away: the M's are removed
the letters at the extremes, first and last

blocks.note: MEN'S EMBLEM, a symbol of masculinity
M, removed from both ends of MENSEMBLEM

annotation.surface: A symbol of masculinity puts off men with extreme views.
annotation.walkthrough: MEN'S EMBLEM happens to begin and end with M, so removing the male (M) extremes leaves ENSEMBLE.
annotation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group acting together, a collective.

entries.clue: Police chief informally to act for The Times in upcoming action (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: to rep is to act as someone's representative
a newspaper refers to itself as 'we', so The Times is US

annotation.surface: A senior police officer taking action on behalf of this very newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's newspaper speaking as 'we' gives US. A super is short for a superintendent, a senior police rank in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Super is the everyday short form of superintendent, a senior police officer.

entries.clue: Ape cutting ends off fruit and eating nut, heading off (5-4)

indicators.note: cutting the ends off trims the last letter from each of the next two words
what eats something takes it inside, so ORANG-AN holds UT
a nut with its heading off has lost its head, the first letter

blocks.note: ORANGE losing its end
NUT losing its heading, N
AND losing its end

annotation.surface: An ape peels fruit and chews a nut.
annotation.walkthrough: ORANG + AN is the outer shell, and it eats UT in the middle. The two-part 'ends off' works on both 'fruit' and 'and'.
annotation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

entries.clue: Switching parts, entered bar (5)

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase change places

blocks.note: entered = GOT IN; the IN part moves to the front
the GOT part moves to the back

annotation.surface: Someone got into a pub by swapping roles.
annotation.walkthrough: Entered is GOT IN; swap its two words to get IN GOT. 'Bar' looks like a pub but is a bar of metal.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, usually gold or silver.

entries.clue: Part of brotherhood now, Keats put up eastern art (9)

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow
in a down clue, putting up means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters sit inside brotherhOOD NOW KEATs, running backwards

annotation.surface: Part of a brotherhood of Romantic poets, with Keats among them, posted up oriental art.
annotation.walkthrough: The Keats reference suggests the Pre-Raphaelite brotherhood, but the words are just a hiding place.
annotation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean martial art, and martial arts are often called eastern arts.

entries.clue: Don’t go drinking Dublin brew, lad (4,2)

indicators.note: one piece swallows another

blocks.note: a lad is a son
tay is the Irish pronunciation and spelling of tea

annotation.surface: A plea to a young man not to leave while drinking Irish ale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brew' suggests Guinness, but here it is a cup of tea, written TAY in Irish dialect.
annotation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain rather than go.

entries.clue: Gets better gadget for making coffee to drink (5,2)

blocks.note: short for percolator
to sup is to drink

annotation.surface: A new coffee machine improves someone's mornings.
annotation.walkthrough: The coffee is apt: coffee is what perks people up.
annotation.definitionFit: To perk up is to become livelier or improve.

entries.clue: Get bigger chaps to replace us in a month (7)

indicators.note: one piece takes another's place

blocks.note: the month; its US is swapped out
chaps are men, going in where US was

annotation.surface: An instruction to recruit more men to swell the ranks for a month.
annotation.walkthrough: AUG-US-T becomes AUG-MEN-T. 'Us' reads as the speaker, but it is just two letters of August.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: augment is a formal word for increase, used of things that grow as well as things made to grow.

entries.clue: Rolled oat mix incapable of fitting in small food processor (5)

indicators.note: turned over: the letters read backwards
the piece named next cannot stay inside

blocks.note: muesli is a breakfast mix of oats
S is short for small; it leaves MUESLI

annotation.surface: Rolled oats won't fit into a little kitchen blender.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small food processor' looks like one gadget, but 'small' belongs to the wordplay and the processor is part of the gut.
annotation.definitionFit: The ileum is the last part of the small intestine, where food is digested and absorbed.

entries.clue: What’ll turn brush to bush just like that (5,4)

blocks.note: R is short for right; take R away from BRUSH and BUSH is left
instantly, without delay

annotation.surface: A gardening puzzle about turning a brush into a bush.
annotation.walkthrough: R is short for right; take it away from BRUSH and BUSH is left.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom pair: 'just like that' and 'right away' both mean instantly, without delay.

entries.clue: Sap, first person fired during argument (10)

indicators.note: inside, as one event sits within another

blocks.note: a debate is an argument; it goes round the rest
I is the first person pronoun
lit means set on fire

annotation.surface: Someone foolish gets sacked in the middle of a row.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sap' reads as a fool and 'fired' as sacked, but sap is the verb to weaken and fired is lit.
annotation.definitionFit: To sap is to drain strength, which is what debilitate means.

entries.clue: Vault subject to court order (5,4)

blocks.note: the verb: to leap over something in one spring
a British court can bind someone over to keep the peace

annotation.surface: A bank vault placed under a court order.
annotation.walkthrough: In British law, someone bound over is ordered by a court to keep the peace. 'Vault' looks like a bank vault but is the verb, to leap.
annotation.definitionFit: To bound over something is to vault it; in British courts, being bound over is an order to keep the peace.

entries.clue: Trade union collecting assorted Euros as fund for union in future? (9)

indicators.note: a union collecting money gathers it in, so TU holds the rest inside
assorted means sorted into a mix, so the letters of 'Euros as' are jumbled

blocks.note: TU is the abbreviation for a trade union; it wraps the rest
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A trade union takes in some euros for a future union fund.
annotation.walkthrough: The two unions differ: the first is a labour union, the one in the definition is a marriage.
annotation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects ahead of her marriage, a stock for a future union.

entries.clue: Recognised author’s work, needing no introduction, one credited with many works (4)

indicators.note: a work needing no introduction has lost its opening, the first letter

blocks.note: an author's canon is their accepted body of work

annotation.surface: A famous author's work, too well known to need introducing.
annotation.walkthrough: Anon, short for anonymous, is credited with countless poems and songs whose authors are unknown.
annotation.definitionFit: Anon is the name printed under works by unknown authors, so it is credited with many.

entries.clue: Long in charge, editor stops caring about details (8)

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so ED plugs the middle of PANT

blocks.note: to pant for something is to long for it
ED is short for editor
I/C is the abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: An editor in charge for too long stops paying attention to detail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops caring' looks like a phrase, but 'stops' is the container and 'caring about details' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedantic person cares excessively about small details.

entries.clue: Drink shot (4)

blocks.note: a noun: a gulp or swig, especially of spirits
the gun sense: a bullet

annotation.walkthrough: Both words have a bar sense and a gun sense: a shot of whisky is a slug of whisky, and a shot from a gun is a slug.
annotation.definitionFit: A slug is a gulp of spirits, and also a bullet, a shot.

entries.clue: Form of water encompassing small river? (6)

annotation.definition: Form of water encompassing small river?

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so STEAM surrounds R

blocks.note: steam is water as vapour
R is short for river

annotation.surface: A body of water that surrounds a little river.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a stream is a small river and a form of water.
annotation.definitionFit: The &lit reading holds: a stream is water in flowing form, and it is exactly what a small river is.

entries.clue: Sellers may be heard here to make public statement (2,2,6)

blocks.note: Peter Sellers, the comic actor, was in the Goons, a 1950s BBC radio comedy team that released records
to state something officially so it can be quoted

annotation.surface: Salespeople are overheard making an official statement.
annotation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers was one of the Goons, the 1950s BBC radio comedy team, so you can hear him on a Goon record. 'Sellers' looks like shopkeepers.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: going on record means stating something officially so it can be quoted, a public statement.

entries.clue: Climbing in the sack, regularly called complete failure (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading bottom to top
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of 'called' is taken

blocks.note: abed means in bed, in the sack
every other letter of CaLlEd

annotation.surface: Getting into bed, someone called it a total flop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The sack' is slang for bed, so 'in the sack' is ABED.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loan word: débâcle first meant the breaking up of river ice, and now means a total collapse or fiasco.

entries.clue: Ropes tied tight and put down again (9)

indicators.note: slang for drunk, so the letters stagger about

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Ropes are tied tight and lowered again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight' seems to describe the knot, but it means drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Built from its parts: RE- means again and deposit means put down.

entries.clue: Fear of god (5)

blocks.note: sudden overwhelming fear
an adjective meaning 'of the Greek god of the wild', formed like 'Homeric' from Homer

annotation.surface: Fear of God.
annotation.walkthrough: Panic is named after Pan, the Greek god who caused sudden terror, so it also means 'of Pan'.
annotation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden fear, and as an adjective it means relating to the god Pan.

entries.clue: Adjust it leftwards somewhat, perhaps, Sir (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Sir, perhaps' read backwards: Sir is an example of a title

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: the letters sit in adjusT IT LEftwards

annotation.surface: An instruction to nudge something a little to the left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leftwards' tempts a solver to read backwards, but the answer runs forwards and 'leftwards' only supplies its last two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sir, the style of a knight, is one kind of title.

entries.clue: German newspaper article backing off-the-cuff remark (2-3)

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so BILD A is read in reverse

blocks.note: Bild is Germany's best-selling tabloid
the indefinite article

annotation.surface: A German paper supports a spontaneous comment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support for the remark, but it reverses BILD + A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin ad libitum, 'at pleasure': an ad-lib is something said without preparation.

entries.clue: Turning up without Scary or Sporty? That’s a disappointment (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: no means without
Scary Spice and Sporty Spice of the Spice Girls were both called Mel

annotation.surface: A Spice Girls reunion without Scary or Sporty would be a letdown.
annotation.walkthrough: Scary Spice was Mel B and Sporty Spice was Mel C, so either one is MEL.
annotation.definitionFit: A lemon is something disappointing or useless, especially a faulty car.

entries.clue: Senior US politician firing judge for a loan (7)

indicators.note: firing someone dismisses them, so J for judge is dismissed from JD VANCE
putting another in its place

blocks.note: JD Vance, US Vice President
J, the abbreviation for judge, is fired
takes J's place

annotation.surface: A senior American politician sacks a judge in exchange for a loan.
annotation.walkthrough: JD Vance is the US Vice President; swap his J for A and he becomes ADVANCE.
annotation.definitionFit: An advance is money paid or lent ahead of time, a loan.

entries.clue: Carry little bug perhaps of symbolic importance (7)

blocks.note: to tote is to carry
a bug is a hidden microphone; mic is its short form

annotation.surface: Carrying a small insect might mean something symbolic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect, but it is a listening device, and 'little' shortens microphone to MIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Totemic means serving as a totem, an emblem of great symbolic importance.

entries.clue: Revival of religious education, basic field of study one’s abandoning (13)

indicators.note: leaving behind: the letter named goes

blocks.note: RE is the British school subject Religious Education
crude means basic
a field of study; it loses I
one is I, which leaves SCIENCE

annotation.surface: A comeback for religious education while a basic subject is dropped.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject, which makes the school-timetable surface convincing.
annotation.definitionFit: Recrudescence is a revival or breaking out again, especially of something unwelcome.
